timeprovider-testable-time.title: Make time-dependent code testable with TimeProvider
timeprovider-testable-time.short: Replace direct clock reads with an injectable time source
timeprovider-testable-time.summary: TimeProvider abstracts the current time and timers so expiry and scheduling logic can be tested without depending on wall-clock time.
timeprovider-testable-time.why: Reading DateTimeOffset.UtcNow throughout a codebase ties tests to real time and makes boundary conditions difficult to reproduce.
timeprovider-testable-time.tips: Inject TimeProvider into services that use time and use a controllable provider in tests to exercise exact expiry boundaries.

periodictimer-single-consumer-loop.title: Run non-overlapping periodic work with PeriodicTimer
periodictimer-single-consumer-loop.short: Own periodic work through one asynchronous wait loop
periodictimer-single-consumer-loop.summary: PeriodicTimer represents periodic work as an asynchronous loop, making sequencing and lifetime easier to follow than callback timers.
periodictimer-single-consumer-loop.why: Starting new work on every tick can overlap executions when one iteration takes longer than the period.
periodictimer-single-consumer-loop.tips: Have one consumer await WaitForNextTickAsync, stop it with cancellation, and define what should happen when work exceeds the configured period.

pipereader-consumed-examined-contract.title: Advance PipeReader consumed and examined positions correctly
pipereader-consumed-examined-contract.short: Distinguish released bytes from bytes already inspected
pipereader-consumed-examined-contract.summary: PipeReader.AdvanceTo reports both consumed and examined positions, controlling buffer retention and when more data should be requested.
pipereader-consumed-examined-contract.why: Incorrect positions can discard required bytes, retain memory unnecessarily, or make incomplete-message reads behave poorly.
pipereader-consumed-examined-contract.tips: Move consumed past fully processed data, move examined past inspected data, and retain incomplete messages for the next read.

memorymarshal-cast-binary-layout.title: Reinterpret binary layouts with MemoryMarshal.Cast
memorymarshal-cast-binary-layout.short: Change a Span element view without copying
memorymarshal-cast-binary-layout.summary: MemoryMarshal.Cast can reinterpret spans of compatible value types and avoid intermediate copies in binary processing.
memorymarshal-cast-binary-layout.why: Ignoring element size, layout, or byte order can interpret the same bytes as unintended values.
memorymarshal-cast-binary-layout.tips: Ensure the types contain no managed references, and prefer explicit BinaryPrimitives reads when a protocol defines byte order.

nativememory-manual-ownership.title: Pair NativeMemory allocation with explicit ownership and release
nativememory-manual-ownership.short: Manage the lifetime of memory outside the GC heap
nativememory-manual-ownership.summary: NativeMemory allocates unmanaged memory that the garbage collector does not release automatically, so ownership must be explicit.
nativememory-manual-ownership.why: Missing a Free path leaks memory, while using a pointer after release can cause corruption beyond normal managed-memory safety.
nativememory-manual-ownership.tips: Establish cleanup immediately with try/finally or an owning wrapper such as SafeHandle and keep raw-pointer sharing narrow.

gc-allocateuninitializedarray-initializa.title: Consider uninitialized arrays when every element is overwritten
gc-allocateuninitializedarray-initializa.short: Avoid zero-initialization only under a strong full-write guarantee
gc-allocateuninitializedarray-initializa.summary: GC.AllocateUninitializedArray can reduce initialization work for arrays whose entire contents are immediately overwritten.
gc-allocateuninitializedarray-initializa.why: Reading any element that was not explicitly written can expose unintended data and violates assumptions provided by normal array allocation.
gc-allocateuninitializedarray-initializa.tips: Use it only on measured hot paths where initialization matters and the code demonstrably overwrites the complete array.

linq-chunk-buffering-boundary.title: Understand the buffering boundary of LINQ Chunk
linq-chunk-buffering-boundary.short: Chunking creates concrete arrays for each batch
linq-chunk-buffering-boundary.summary: Chunk groups an enumeration into arrays of bounded size, which is useful for batching downstream work and I/O.
linq-chunk-buffering-boundary.why: Each chunk is an allocated array, so treating it as allocation-free deferred enumeration can add pressure on large workloads.
linq-chunk-buffering-boundary.tips: Choose a batch size appropriate for the downstream operation and preserve bounded streaming when processing large sources.

configureawait-library-boundary.title: Define a ConfigureAwait policy at library boundaries
configureawait-library-boundary.short: Know whether continuations require the caller's synchronization context
configureawait-library-boundary.summary: ConfigureAwait(false) states that an await continuation does not require the current synchronization context.
configureawait-library-boundary.why: Mixing context-dependent UI code with context-independent library code can create unnecessary scheduling and invalid thread assumptions.
configureawait-library-boundary.tips: Keep reusable libraries independent of caller context where practical, while preserving context in layers that explicitly require it for UI or similar work.

httpclient-defaultrequestheaders-mutatio.title: Do not mutate shared HttpClient headers per request
httpclient-defaultrequestheaders-mutatio.summary: DefaultRequestHeaders are defaults for a shared HttpClient, not a per-request storage location for changing user or operation state.
httpclient-defaultrequestheaders-mutatio.why: Concurrent requests can race with shared header mutation and send another request's authentication or tracing values.
httpclient-defaultrequestheaders-mutatio.tips: Keep stable defaults on the client and set request-specific authorization, tracing, and similar headers on each HttpRequestMessage.

unity-nativearray-reinterpret-layout.title: Check binary layout before reinterpreting a Unity NativeArray
unity-nativearray-reinterpret-layout.short: Zero-copy type views require compatible element layout
unity-nativearray-reinterpret-layout.summary: NativeArray Reinterpret can expose the same native storage through another element type, avoiding conversion copies in low-level paths.
unity-nativearray-reinterpret-layout.why: Incorrect assumptions about element size or layout can change element counts and interpret boundaries incorrectly.
unity-nativearray-reinterpret-layout.tips: Verify source and destination sizes, alignment, and data format; use normal conversion when value conversion rather than representation reinterpretation is intended.
